name: Matter correspondence and attendance notes
one_line: REFUSED. "Letters, emails and notes of calls and meetings exchanged in the course of one matter" names two entries of the law_practice schema's own work_type enum ("client instructions, attendance note and matter correspondence"; "counsel and third-party professional correspondence") plus two SOURCE_TYPES (email, text_document). Its detection signals are the schema's deterministic signal 11 and needs_llm signal 5 restated; its dimension_order is the schema's empty order; its privacy posture is the schema's third-party posture, and nothing in it is stricter than the privilege-log rule the schema already carries. All three legs of the node test return identical-to-default. The coverage is absorbed by the law_practice schema itself, whose first grouping reason already names the correspondence as a member of the one-matter group, and by four named siblings for the correspondence classes that DO have their own structure.
refuse_reason:
Fails all three legs of CONNECTION.md's node test against its own schema's default template, and fails them for three independent reasons.

LEG 1 - DETECTION SIGNALS ARE NOT DIFFERENT, THEY ARE THE SAME SENTENCES. The law_practice schema's deterministic list already carries the whole of the correspondence half: "AN EMAIL or CALENDAR record whose structured slots tie it to an ALREADY EVIDENCED matter: labelled sender and recipient roles crossing the practitioner-client or counsel boundary, a subject carrying the exact matter reference, an organizer and attendee set separating practitioner, client, counsel and tribunal." The schema's needs_llm list already carries the whole of the attendance-note half: "Recognising unlabelled practitioner prose - an attendance note, a file note of a telephone call, a strategy email in running text, a handwritten-then-scanned advice note." A template whose signals are its parent schema's signals quoted back is the schema's default template with a narrower filename filter - the exact thing the schema itself warns 36 template authors against.

LEG 2 - THE DIMENSION ORDER CANNOT DIFFER AND, IF IT COULD, THE ONE DIFFERENCE THIS ROW WOULD CLAIM IS FORBIDDEN. Under PR-6 the schema declares no fields, so dimension_order is [] here and [] on the default; identical by contract. The only substantive order this row could argue for is time_first, because a correspondence file is genuinely a chronological stream in practice - and the schema forecloses it family-wide on 00's own words, "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." So the one axis on which this row is not a duplicate is an axis it is not permitted to occupy.

LEG 3 - PRIVACY IS THE SCHEMA'S, NOT STRICTER. Correspondence bodies carry a third party's affairs, which is exactly the interest the schema was built to protect - it "protects a THIRD PARTY's - a client, an adverse party, a witness, a deponent, an accused, a child - who never chose this filesystem and cannot consent." A mail thread is not more sensitive than the privilege log the schema already fixtures, which is a table of thousands of other people's correspondence metadata. Same posture, same sensitivity value, no new rule.

AND THE ROW IS ALSO THE THING THE CHARGE NAMES DIRECTLY. "Letters" and "emails" are a medium; "notes of calls and meetings" is a document type; "exchanged in the course of one matter" is the schema's own matter anchor. Strip the medium, the document-type words and the anchor, and nothing structural survives - the deletion test the schema imports from business_operations.organisational-records. What is left of the attendance note after the strip is an artefact defined by ABSENCE: alone in this family it has no labelled slot, no caption, no execution block and no column set, and its only tie to a matter is a reference written in a corner. A row whose distinguishing property is that its files have no structure cannot supply detection signals; it can only inherit membership from an anchor established elsewhere, which is P9 grouping, not template activation.

CONSEQUENCE, NOT A GAP. Refusing costs no coverage. The schema's first grouping reason already enumerates this material - "ONE MATTER from opening to closure, joined by an exact repeated matter reference: the intake screen, the opening record, the engagement terms, the correspondence, the work product, the filings, the disclosure, the billing and the closure record" - so a matter letter or attendance note is a member of a group the schema already licenses, on the schema's own activation. The correspondence classes that DO carry their own structure are already owned by siblings that were given them for that structure: instructions to and opinions from counsel (law_practice.opinions-advice, on the schema's two-professional-role front sheet), without-prejudice offer and settlement traffic (law_practice.settlement), first client instructions at the point of opening (law_practice.client-intake), and the engagement terms letter itself (law_practice.engagement-terms). What remains after those four is ordinary mail, and ordinary mail is a SOURCE_TYPE.

never_alone: STATED FOR THE REFUSAL RECORD, NOT AS THIS ROW'S RECOGNITION - the schema owns recognition and this row authors none. AN EMAIL, A LETTER OR A NOTE FROM A LAW-FIRM SENDER OR ON LAW-FIRM LETTERHEAD, ALONE. This is the token that makes the row look researchable and it discriminates nothing: a firm domain sends client mail, opposing-counsel mail, marketing newsletters, recruitment mail, invoices for the firm's own supplies, and mail to the firm's own lawyers about their own affairs. It is the schema's struck firm-name token wearing an envelope.

A DOCUMENT-TYPE WORD FOR A MESSAGE OR A NOTE - letter, email, correspondence, memo, note, attendance note, file note, telephone note, minute, RE:, FW:. These are the row's entire name and they are values of the schema's work_type enum. 00's own construction is that a work type is meaningful only after its parent is known: "A work type such as Homework 3 is meaningful only after the course is known." An attendance note is Homework 3.

A FOLDER OR ARCHIVE MEMBER PATH NAMED Correspondence, Letters, Emails or Notes. This is the purest evidence that the id is a label rather than a node - the row's name is the name practitioners give a DRAWER, and 00 governs it: "A session should never be treated as proof of topic." A drawer is a position, not a fact.
SOURCE TYPE email OR A .eml/.msg/.mbox EXTENSION. file_kind_plausible is constitutionally never-alone, and the row's medium half rests entirely on it.

A WITHOUT-PREJUDICE, PRIVILEGED, CONFIDENTIAL or SUBJECT-TO-CONTRACT LEGEND ON A MESSAGE. Preserved as a literal observation, never a legal status and never activation - and where it is genuine settlement traffic the anchor is law_practice.settlement's, not a correspondence row's.
A MATTER-SHAPED TOKEN IN A SUBJECT LINE, ALONE. Linkage after a labelled role is established, never before it, and never a date from its digits.

template.why: Empty because the row is refused, and empty for the same three reasons the schema's own order is empty - contract (PR-6 declares no fields, so no field can be branched on), safety (this material co-activates `legal`, and "Finance, identity, medical, and legal material should be implemented first as safety domains, meaning the system detects and protects them before any cloud or automated placement decision is allowed."), and disclosure (a branch named for a client or a matter publishes the representation). The row's one candidate difference from the default order was time_first, and the schema forecloses it: "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." Whatever a future order becomes, it stays advisory - "the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions."

file_kinds.note: Recorded so the refusal is auditable, not to claim ownership. This list is a subset of the law_practice schema's own file_kinds and adds nothing to it - which is itself part of the refusal argument.

one attachment named as a draft offer letter

The schema already sees this file completely, and a template that adds nothing to what the schema sees is the schema's default template

that the WITHOUT PREJUDICE legend activates anything, or decides privilege, admissibility or waiver. Where the offer traffic is genuinely the subject, the anchor is law_practice.settlement's structural one, not a medium row's

The schema already books it under needs_llm - "Recognising unlabelled practitioner prose - an attendance note, a file note of a telephone call" - and 00 already books the class generally, since real collections contain "unlabeled forms, unusual professional artifacts"
that the matter reference in the header activates the schema by itself; an identifier supplies linkage only after a labelled role is established

sensitivity_why: Recorded even on a refusal, because the refusal must not downgrade anything. Matter letters, attendance notes and mail bodies describe a third party's affairs, and the schema that absorbs them is built on that exact interest - it protects someone "who never chose this filesystem and cannot consent." The material co-activates `legal`, one of 00's four safety domains, and 00 licenses protection without a group: rare but sensitive legal documents "may be surfaced as protected records even when they do not meet a normal group-size threshold." Only `potentially_sensitive` is available in this phase; P7 owns handling classes and none is assigned.
open_question: Four items for R1c, none of which changes the refusal. (1) RECIPROCITY DEBT: `business_operations.meeting-record` names this id one-way in both its JSON and its memo - "an attendance note of a client or counsel meeting" - and that edge now dangles. Recommend R1c re-point it at the `law_practice` SCHEMA, whose needs_llm 4 already states the same seam from the other side (the firm running itself versus the firm running a matter); this row may not edit a neighbour. (2) If PR-6 lifts and `project` (the schema's declined-to-mint matter anchor) is adopted, re-test this id once: a correspondence row would still be a work_type value, so the expected answer is unchanged, but the test should be run rather than assumed. (3) A correspondence stream is the one artefact class in this family that is genuinely chronological in practice, and the schema forbids time_first family-wide. Joseph should decide whether the family's blanket prohibition is right, or whether a stream-shaped member may be ordered by period BELOW an anchor level - a question about the schema, not about this id. (4) Decide where a matter attendance note with no reference at all should sit when a matter neighbourhood exists but no anchor does: Protected Records (protective, but files an unproven association) or Review Later (honest, but leaves third-party prose outside the protected set). This row recommends Review Later for the unreadable and unanchored case and Protected Records once any accepted matter group is active, and flags that the two residuals have different safety consequences.
